Adjusted summary using the April 2021 Beige Book insights:

- Policy stance: FOMC kept the policy rate at 0–0.25% and continued asset purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B agency MBS) with outcome-based forward guidance (maximum employment; inflation moderately above 2% for some time).
- Beige Book corroboration: National activity was picking up, with consumer spending and tourism improving as vaccinations progressed. Hiring strengthened notably in manufacturing, construction, and leisure/hospitality, though labor availability remained a challenge for low-wage, hourly, and skilled trades. Wage pressures were building in tighter segments. Price increases were reported, with cost pressures tied to supply-chain disruptions and winter weather—consistent with the FOMC’s “largely transitory” inflation framing.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS lens): Banks eased standards across residential real estate and consumer credit; some easing for investment-grade C&I at large banks, while riskier C&I remained tighter than pre-pandemic. Demand was softer for C&I but firmer for mortgages/household credit. This supports the accommodative stance while highlighting uneven credit access by borrower risk.
- Net read: Beige Book evidence of broadening demand (including tourism) and vaccination-boosted employment tilts the tone more positive than a purely financial-stability/SLOOS view, though uneven labor supply, lingering virus risks, and cost pressures warrant caution.
